title: Conservativity of geometric stalks on the derived category
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and let $K\to L$ be a morphism of complexes in
$\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then $K\to L$ is an
isomorphism of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ if and only if for every geometric point
[def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] $\bar t$ of $T$ and every integer $i$ the
induced map

$$
 \mathcal H^i(K)_{\bar t}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^i(L)_{\bar t}
$$

of geometric stalks is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\Ab(T_{\Et})$. By [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], $D^+(T_{\Et})$ is a strictly full subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$, so invertibility of a morphism between its objects is the same in these two categories. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the functors $H^i$ on $D(\mathcal A)$ factor the cohomology of complexes, and a complex map is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when all its $H^i$ maps are invertible. For a complex map $f$, if all $H^i(f)$ are invertible, then $Q(f)$ is invertible by localization. Conversely, if $Q(f)$ is invertible, applying each functor $H^i$ shows $H^i(f)$ invertible. This criterion also holds for an arbitrary derived morphism $u$: the calculus of fractions in [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] writes it as $Q(f)\circ Q(s)^{-1}$ for a roof $K\xleftarrow{s}M\xrightarrow{f}L$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $H^i(f)=H^i(u)\circ H^i(s)$ under the stated factorization identifications. If every $H^i(u)$ is invertible, $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $u^{-1}=Q(s)\circ Q(f)^{-1}$. The reverse implication follows by applying the functors $H^i$ to $u$ and its inverse.

proof.text: Assume all displayed maps are isomorphisms. For each integer $i$, $H^i(u)$ is a morphism in the abelian etale sheaf category of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], by [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Its geometric stalk maps are exactly the maps in the hypothesis; no interchange of stalks with cohomology of a stalk complex is needed because the display already takes the stalk of the cohomology sheaf. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $H^i(u)$: it is an isomorphism of sheaves. Step 1 then proves $u$ invertible in $D^+(T_{\Et})$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph; apply sheaf conservativity directly to the displayed cohomology-sheaf maps

proof.text: If $u$ is invertible, the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] carry $u$ and its inverse to mutually inverse sheaf maps $H^i(u)$ and $H^i(u^{-1})$. Taking the geometric stalks of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] carries their two identity composites to identity composites: the maps of stalks are induced by the maps on sections in the defining colimit, which respect identity and composition. Hence each displayed stalk map is an isomorphism, with inverse the stalk of $H^i(u^{-1})$.
